newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Derivative trade seen supporting Brussels bourse.
newsitem.headline: Derivative trade seen supporting Brussels bourse.

text.p: The Brussels bourse outperformed neighbouring markets on Wednesday and could continue to do so if options-linked trades continue to support prices, dealers said.

The Bel-20 index bounced back sharply from session lows hit after the Dow Jones index and dollar took a dive in early New York trading to end the day just 0.56 percent lower at 1,871.55 points, near its high for the day.
Amsterdam's AEX index slipped 1.89 percent, Paris CAC-40 lost 1.69 percent and Germany's DAX closed 1.73 percent lower.
"We saw some (Bel-20) basket buying. I think one big player does not want the index to slip," one trader said.
The next Belfox Bel-20 options expiry on December 20 will be the most significant of the year, after which steel maker electronics group Barco will enter, she noted.

Another trader believed two or three of the bigger players were seeking to influence the index level. He said, however, that it was more likely due to over-the-counter options rather than exchange-traded products.
"We have seen for the last couple of weeks that Brussels is not really moving with the other European markets, although the absence of foreign investors could also be a reason," he said.
Barco was among the heaviest traded shares, ending 50 francs lower at 5,440 on a report major shareholder, Belgian holding company Asphales, was seeking to reduce its stake.
One trader noted Asphales' stake has fallen from more than five percent in June to a little over four percent this week, according to transparency declarations filed with the bourse.
"I think they are still selling in the market, but they have said they don't want to sell all the stock," she said.
Bank Dexia CC was also heavily traded for the third day in a row, ending down 55 francs at 2,750.
Investors were switching out of Dexia to buy shares in French partner bank Credit Local de France ahead of a special dividend payment by CLF next week, one trader said.
The payment was announced earlier this year ahead of the two banks' cross-border alliance as a way of equalising their equity.
"There's some arbitrage going on between the two...probably people will switch back to Dexia after the dividend," he said.
